Suppose the category <MATH_0001> and
the functor <MATH_0002>
have the following properties:
<STRUCT_0001>

<STRUCT_0004> the functor <MATH_0006> reflects isomorphisms.
<STRUCT_0005>
Let <MATH_0007> be a topological space. Let <MATH_0008>
be a presheaf with values in <MATH_0009>.
Then <MATH_0010> is a sheaf if and only if the
underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf.

Assume that <MATH_0001> is a sheaf. Then
<MATH_0002> is the equalizer of the diagram
above and by assumption we see <MATH_0003>
is the equalizer of the corresponding diagram
of sets. Hence <MATH_0004> is a sheaf of sets.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume that <MATH_0005> is a sheaf.
Let <MATH_0006> be the
equalizer of the two parallel arrows in
Definition <REF_0001>.
We get a canonical morphism <MATH_0007>,
simply because <MATH_0008> is a presheaf.
By assumption, the induced map <MATH_0009>
is an isomorphism, because <MATH_0010> is the equalizer
of the corresponding diagram of sets. Hence we
see <MATH_0011> is an isomorphism
by condition (3) of the lemma.

<STRUCT_0001>
The lemma in particular applies to
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>sheaves of groups, rings, algebras over a fixed ring, modules
over a fixed ring, vector spaces over a fixed field, <TEXTITCLOSE_0001> etc.
In other words, these are presheaves of groups, rings,
modules over a fixed ring, vector spaces over a fixed field, etc
such that the underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf.
